Time limits of a call to the register

register_timeouts.Rd

One minute for a call and ten seconds to connect, the connection as for the module (module_timeouts()).

Usage

register_timeouts()

Value

A list with total and connect, in seconds.

Details

The register lives on a REDCap instance like the others, and an update of the fleet, a table change that holds the readings, is the typical case of a connection taken and no answer. Its calls are short: a read of the event log takes a fraction of a second, and the whole report, which reads the rows and the log, a few seconds. A minute is far more than the read of the log.

Not the five minutes of the module, because the register is asked many times in a round and every question costs its own wait. A register that hangs after the round has read the rows makes it wait at most nine times (the log of the creations, the log of the owners, the identities, the outcome, the owner twice, the Entra account twice, the seals), plus one for every row whose log is read on its own, and the report twice plus one per row: with five minutes the round would reach the three hours of its unit with 27 such rows, and the report its hour with 10; with one minute the report reaches it with 58.

A write that runs out of time may have been carried out, and the answer be what was lost. The round writes to the register after the mail ("send first, write after", see provisioning_reconcile()), and the next round computes again what the register is told from the instances' state, so nothing is granted twice. What it costs: the code goes into errori and the alarm on outcomes not written sounds, whether or not the write had arrived; when it had not, the next round sends the outcome message again.
